title: Table Fellowship
lead: Table fellowship means sharing a meal as a sign of acceptance. In the ancient world, who ate with whom marked who belonged. For Jews, eating with Gentiles raised questions of food laws, ritual purity and idolatry, and for the early churches these questions came to a head at Antioch (Galatians 2:11-14), in Peter's visit to Cornelius (Acts 10:28; 11:3) and in the meals at Corinth (1 Corinthians 8-10; 11:17-34).

sections.b: Jesus was criticized for eating with sinners (Mark 2:16). Peter was criticized for eating with uncircumcised men (Acts 11:3). At Antioch, Cephas ate with the Gentile believers until people came from James, and then drew back (Galatians 2:12). Scholars disagree whether the issue was food the Torah forbids, ritual purity, food and wine tied to idols, or the rule that Gentiles must become Jews to be full members of the table (Dunn, Nanos, Fredriksen, Esler).
